what_worked: Strong thesis about hidden concentration; excellent data-quality slide; clean visual hierarchy throughout.
fix_next: Aggregate MRR is $15.6M not $13.5M; the 5.7× B2B claim uses means not medians (actual median ratio ≈2.35×); verify every headline number.
verdict: Well-structured narrative undermined by several material numerical errors.
factual_error_detail: Slide 1: Aggregate MRR stated as $13.5M; actual total 30-day revenue is $15,596,344.59. Slide 2: '5.7× more monthly revenue for B2B vs B2C' — reference median multiples are ~2.35× (B2B) and ~2.30× (B2C); even the median ratio is about 5.7× only if using non-standard medians ($1,036/$181), but the reference B2B/B2C median revenue multiples are 2.35×/2.30×, suggesting the $1,036/$181 figures on slide 6 are not aligned with the frozen dataset. Slide 2: '48% of all revenue earned by top 1%' — top-10 share is 49.6%, so top 1% (10 startups) earning 48% is close but slightly understated. Slide 4: Top 10% share stated as 81.8% — not directly verifiable but plausible extrapolation; top-10 share is 49.6% so this is a different cut. Slide 7: Category medians diverge from reference — AI median shown as $446 vs reference $503; Education shown as $2,142 vs reference $2,435; Marketing shown as $1,586 vs reference $2,369.50; SaaS shown as $303 vs reference $200.50; Content Creation shown as $1,254 vs reference $1,237.50. Multiple category medians are materially off. Slide 10: Stealth median $7,337 — 40× claim; anonymous share of revenue is 26.5% which is about 2× their population share, not 40× in median terms without verification.

evidence.insight: Slide 7's AI-crowding insight is genuinely useful; slide 10's stealth-company observation is interesting; slide 9's listed-for-sale growth deceleration is a non-obvious finding. However, several insights rest on incorrect numbers.
evidence.narrative: Clear numbered progression from concentration → growth → audience → category → channels → marketplace → visibility → pricing → recommendations. Coherent thesis about hidden winners. Landing slide synthesizes for two audiences.
evidence.framing: Slide 3 handles missingness well with a clear threshold rule. Audience (founders and investors) stated on slide 12. However, no explicit mention that this is self-reported/survivorship-biased data beyond the subtitle.
evidence.accuracy: Aggregate revenue wrong by ~$2M (slide 1). B2B/B2C multiplier headline claim doesn't match reference medians. Multiple category medians diverge materially from reference. The 20% zero-revenue claim is close (216/1000=21.6%). Country missing 24% matches reference 241/1000=24.1%. Category missing 27% matches 274/1000=27.4%.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark-navy/orange palette, clean chart labeling, good use of callout stats alongside charts, appropriate chart types (horizontal bars, vertical bars). Slight template sameness across slides but functional. Legible hierarchy.
evidence.ai_slop: Mild template repetition (every slide uses identical layout: chart left, three callout stats right), but content is substantive and specific to the dataset. No generic filler text. The consulting-style 'Four Numbers That Define This Market' is slightly inflated but backed by data.
